1Discuss Lola’s situation

Lola is planning to resign. Concha, who is giving her advice, thinks the company will try hard to keep her.

1How do you think the company is going to react to Lola’s resignation?
2Will she be able to leave on good terms? What could she do to make that happen?
3Have you ever resigned from a company?
4Have you ever walked away from a project or a team? What made you decide to leave?
5What is it to be ruthless?
6Have you ever worked for a ruthless manager?
7What is a dog-eat-dog world?
8Did you feel you were working in a dog-eat-dog world? How competitive was the industry?
Teacher: Show the questions and let her speak first. Explain the expressions only afterwards.

4Choose the preposition

Getting into a vehicle or onto it. Tap each form of transport to choose: get on or get in / into.

What pattern do you notice?

get on: you can stand up or walk around inside, or you sit on top (horse, bicycle, bus, plane, train, ship, spaceship). get in / into: small, closed spaces where you sit down (car, taxi, canoe, kayak, space capsule).

Teacher: Ask her to group the vehicles first and say what pattern she notices.

Your situation

You’re joining a global Visa forum. Some colleagues are meeting you for the first time. Introduce yourself in 20–30 seconds so they understand where you work, who you work with, and what you help them do.

00:00

Notes board

1Practice four useful terms

Vocabulary

customer segmentation

segmentação de clientes

We use customer segmentation to understand how different groups of customers use digital banking services.

Vocabulary

digital channels

canais digitais

We help banks improve the customer experience across their digital channels, including their apps and websites.

Phrasal verb

roll out

lançar ou implementar

We helped a bank roll out a new onboarding process in its mobile app.

Phrasal verb

scale up

ampliar o alcance ou a operação

After the pilot, the bank decided to scale up the initiative and offer it to more customers.

From pilot to rollout

Read the story. Tap the underlined words for their meaning in English.

A bank wanted to make it easier for new customers to open an account. First, the team tested a simpler onboarding process with a small group. The pilot worked well, so the bank decided to roll out the new process in its mobile app. Then, using customer segmentation, the team saw which groups of customers used the app the most. Because the results were so good, the bank decided to scale up the initiative: it offered the simpler process to more customer groups and added it to other digital channels, such as its website.

Answer using the new words:

1What did the bank roll out, and where?
2What did the team use customer segmentation for?
3How did the bank scale up the initiative?
4Which digital channels are mentioned?
5Now tell a similar story: what could a bank roll out? What could it scale up?
Show answers (1–4)

1) The simpler onboarding process, in its mobile app. 2) To see which groups of customers used the app the most. 3) It offered the process to more customer groups and added it to other digital channels. 4) The mobile app and the website.

Teacher: Read the story together first, then ask the questions so she uses roll out and scale up.
